Field Detail

useSplinesForZTmapping

public static final boolean useSplinesForZTmapping
Flag to indicate Z,->t mapping. Tests indicate that Splines for the ZT mapping can cause serious flapping of the map if the sequence of points is not especially smooth (as can happen under possible configurations of the stochastic model): the usual spline-kicking phenomenon. Linear mapping (which is used if this is off) tends to be more robust under these circumstances.

See Also:
Constant Field Values

RIGOROUSLY_EXCLUDE_EDGE_REGIONS

public static final boolean RIGOROUSLY_EXCLUDE_EDGE_REGIONS
Flag to indicate rigorous exclusion of window edge regions polluted by padding etc. Tests indicate that this is necessary to prevent discontinuities in the objective function caused by reflections wandering in and out of the (_WE.tStart,_WE.tEnd) inversion interval. These discontinuities are large and seriously distress the minimiser.

Excluding edge regions means also that the number of data points in the likelihood will vary as the wavelet span is changed, and the Bayesian machinery doesn't cope very well with this. For this reason, we set the range of data in the likelihood to be the smallest which will be seen by any of the wavelets

See Also:

WRITE_REFLECTIVITIES_TO_TRUE_PLUS_SYNTH_FILES

public static final boolean WRITE_REFLECTIVITIES_TO_TRUE_PLUS_SYNTH_FILES
Set this to be true if you want the true (first trace) and synthetic (second trace) SU files to include reflectivity in the third trace as well

writeOutTrueAndSyntheticSUset

void writeOutTrueAndSyntheticSUset(java.lang.String prefix)

Strawman: write out SU versions of current synthetics, spanning transverse range ample enough range to cover well range. Makes sense to call after computeSyntheticNegLogLikelihood() has been called with sane variables in place. The files written will have true and synthetic traces written to adjacent traces:

Traces appear in this order:

(1) true seismic
(2) synthetic seismic
(3) (maybe) reflectivity
(4) (maybe) X values
(5) (maybe) Y values

There are distinct files for each stack & each well.
